thread:
Alex (Support): FYI customer 'acme' opened an escalation. They see a big P99 latency spike and intermittent 401s.
Customer console shows region badge eu-west-1 but request traces show responses served from us-east-1. Escalating to eng/SRE.

Maria (Customer Success): Customer report: p50 ~60ms normally -> p99 ~430-500ms since 03:14 UTC. Seeing some 401s with same API key. Billing flagged unexpected cross-region egress.

Jason (Eng-Routing): Can you paste one request_id and full response headers? Also are these only from specific client IP ranges? @Sam (SRE) ping.

Alex (Support): Request id: req_000abcd1234
Sample response headers from their capture:

    x-request-id: req_000abcd1234
    x-region-preference: eu-west-1
    x-served-pop: us-east-1
    x-auth-status: ok
    x-fallback-reason: capacity_shortage

And trace excerpt from our trace service for req_000abcd1234:

```
trace_id: 000abcd1234
steps:
 - edge: eu-west-1 (preferred)
 - route_decision: fallback_to us-east-1
 - backend: serving-node-112.us-east-1
latency_ms_total: 428
fallback_reason: capacity_shortage
```

Sam (SRE): I can repro from our side with the same header. Running quick check on eu-west-1 pool:

```
$ infra-popctl status --pop eu-west-1
active_serving_nodes: 0
queued_burst_slots: 12
available_slots: 0
```

Sam (SRE): So config allows fallback to other POPs when available slots == 0. That explains serve-from us-east. But console badge should show final served pop, not preferred. Looks like UI is reading customer preferred pop metadata rather than resolve result.

telemetry-bot: trace:req_000abcd1234 | p95=430ms | served_pop=us-east-1 | console_label=eu-west-1 | fallback=capacity_shortage

deploy-bot: Note: config change to routing policy 'allow_cross_pop_fallback=true' rolled out 2d ago to improve availability.

Jason (Eng-Routing): Root cause looks twofold:
 - eu-west capacity exhausted -> automated fallback to us-east
 - Console surface bug: UI shows request-level region preference or assigned route, not final serving POP

Immediate mitigations:
 - We can pin that customer to eu-west dedicated route (temporary) or set prefer_local=false to avoid deceptive UI labeling.
 - SRE can flush auth cache on us-east nodes in case 401s were caused by stale key replication.

Maria (Customer Success): Repro steps I used (customer provided):

```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_acme_***" \
  -H "x-region-preference: eu-west-1" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-large","input":"hi"}'

Response headers included:
  x-served-pop: us-east-1
  x-request-id: req_000abcd1234
```

Alex (Support): Customer also worried about billing since egress and compute are charged by serving region. They saw a single-hour spike billed at us-east rates.

Sam (SRE): I inspected auth logs on us-east serving-node-112 and found intermittent cache misses causing 401s for that key. I flushed the key cache and restarted auth-sync on the node.

Sam (SRE): After flush, I re-ran the curl repro and got 200 consistently. Telemetry shows p95 dropped to ~180ms for the next hour but still served from us-east until eu-west capacity returns.

Jason (Eng-Routing): UX action: change console label to show two fields: preferred_region (what client requested) and served_region (final POP from traces). Also we should add a tooltip explaining fallback behavior and billing implications.

Maria (Customer Success): Customer accepted pinning to eu-west until capacity is replenished. Please confirm when done and we'll close the loop.

Sam (SRE): I filed infra ticket INFRA-9832 to add capacity to eu-west and a short lived override to prevent fallback for pinned customers. Pin request for acme submitted.

Jason (Eng-Routing): I'll open a quick UI bug (ENG-UI-1227) to swap the label to served_region. Also adding a trace-link in the console pointing directly to the trace service so customers can verify.

Alex (Support): Thanks all — passing mitigation to customer. Will update once INFRA ticket progresses.

Maria (Customer Success): Thanks team :thumbsup:
